clue.text: It's satisfying that joy returns when grub's around

indicators.note: around means the word for grub wraps itself about the other piece on both sides

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word for joy is read right to left

parts.note: glee is great joy

explanation.surface: A hungry person is delighted when the food finally comes round.
explanation.definitionFit: A feelgood film or song is one that leaves you contented and cheerful, which is what satisfying describes.

clue.text: Budgetary bluff is called, partly at least!

indicators.note: partly says that only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters span all three words

explanation.surface: A poker player's bluff over the budget is exposed, to some degree anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal relates to government revenue and spending, the subject of a budget.

clue.text: I remove marks ages before the Queen

parts.note: eras are long ages of history
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch who has been erasing traces of the past for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person, as if the object were speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber, whose whole purpose is to take pencil marks off paper.

clue.text: Crime boss at a christening?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the head of a Mafia family
second meaning: a male sponsor who stands for the child at baptism

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the second half being a description of where you find this person rather than a straight synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia chief and the baptismal sponsor share one title, made famous by the film about the Corleone family.

clue.text: A kind of blue way to a London shopping centre

parts.note: Oxford blue is a dark blue, the university's colour
a street is a way or road

explanation.surface: Directions to the shops given in terms of a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford Street is London's busiest shopping street, in the West End.
explanation.definitionFit: The street is lined with department stores and is a major retail hub of the capital.

clue.text: Best hint? On the contrary! First class!

indicators.note: on the contrary tells you to turn the phrase just built around, putting its second word before its first

parts.note: a tip is a hint or piece of advice
top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Someone offers a best hint and is promptly contradicted, then praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' does not reverse letters here: it flips the order of the two words that 'Best hint' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal adjective for excellent or of the highest quality, the same idea as first-rate.

clue.text: Rachmaninoff's ending played in the billiard hall?

indicators.note: the ending of a name is its final stretch of letters, taken as they stand

parts.note: the last five letters of the composer's name

explanation.surface: The close of a Rachmaninov piece performed in a snooker club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' suggests music, but it means a shot played on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-off is a billiards or snooker shot where the ball goes into a pocket after striking another ball.

clue.text: It's great to get up cold, if it covers boob

indicators.note: covers means one piece goes around another on both sides
in a down entry getting up means rising from bottom to top, so letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a boob is a blunder, so to boob is to err
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cheerful claim that getting up in the cold is great, if it hides a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-letter words it and if are turned around; it then wraps the word for boob, and cold is tacked on last.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific is an informal adjective for excellent, the everyday sense of great.

clue.text: Teaching's soft and tense, since being retained

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: something retained is held inside, so the word for since is kept within another

parts.note: edgy means nervous or tense
ago and since both refer back in time, as in 'long ago' and 'long since'

explanation.surface: A teacher's style described as gentle yet strained ever since being kept on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like grammar in a clue about teaching, but it means nervy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedagogy is the method and practice of teaching, the theory behind instruction.

clue.text: Rugby player to keep away

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the half-back who links the scrum half to the three-quarters
second meaning: a phrasal verb for keeping your distance

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the stand-off, also called the fly-half, is the player who receives the ball from the scrum half.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby position takes its name from standing off the scrum, and the phrasal verb means remaining at a distance.

clue.text: I am behind the bishop in the coal-scuttle, which is awful

indicators.note: in puts the joined pieces inside the coal-carrying container

parts.note: a hod is a scuttle for carrying coal

indicators.note: behind places one piece directly after the other in the reading order

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
I is the subject of 'I am'

explanation.surface: A confession of sitting behind a bishop inside a coal bucket, which is awful indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is the standard crossword bishop; a hod is a container for carrying coal or bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrid is a common, slightly childish synonym for nasty or dreadful, matching awful.

clue.text: Grand argument to get her to close ranks

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a row is a noisy quarrel
taken as written, run together

explanation.surface: A big quarrel used to win a woman over before the group unites.
explanation.definitionFit: To close ranks is to unite in solidarity, the same as joining up and becoming one.

clue.text: Place of activity, partly for those with bare navels!

indicators.note: partly says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A venue that suits the crop-top crowd who show off their midriffs.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a field or sphere of action, literally a stadium and figuratively any scene of activity.

clue.text: Reorganisation of RAF in grey, becoming thinner

indicators.note: a reorganisation rearranges what is there, so the following letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An air-force shake-up of grey-uniformed ranks leaves them thinning out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rarefy is to make or grow less dense, so rarefying is the gas or air growing thinner.

clue.text: Suggestion of words being composed on behalf of the author

definitions.text: being composed on behalf of the author

parts.note: a ghost is a faint trace or suggestion, as in the ghost of a smile
writing is words set down on a page

explanation.surface: A hint that a famous author's words were really produced by somebody else.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghostwriting is producing a book or speech that is published under another person's name.

clue.text: Candle: I need it to crumble just the same

indicators.note: crumbling breaks a thing into pieces, so the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants their candle to fall apart in exactly the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike in every detail, which is what just the same expresses.

clue.text: Show Lily dancing in a solemn way

indicators.note: dancing moves around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to demonstrate a girl's dance with a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are proverbially wise and grave-looking, so acting owlishly is looking solemn and studious.

clue.text: King''s Cross and Euston — there's more than one calling here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two London railway termini, examples of the answer

definitions.text: there's more than one calling here
definitions.meaning: second meaning: plural of a word for one's calling or position in life, and trains call at them

explanation.walkthrough: King's Cross and Euston are neighbouring London mainline railway terminals; a station is also one's rank or calling, as in 'above your station'.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway stops share the word with social positions or vocations, so the plural fits both readings.

clue.text: Distributed reward of poet to prevent from getting wet

definitions.note: the answer is a past participle, the definition an infinitive

indicators.note: distributed things are spread about, so the letters are scattered into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet's prize money is handed out to keep it from getting soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and answer do not quite agree in form: the answer is a past tense, the clue an infinitive.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterproof something is to treat it so rain cannot soak through, keeping it dry.

clue.text: A small demon seen in a hat, which is transparent

indicators.note: seen in places the little devil inside the headwear

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
an imp is a small mischievous demon

explanation.surface: A little devil spotted wearing a see-through hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid describes water or air that is clear enough to see through, so it means transparent.

clue.text: Law, say, is involved on every occasion

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The law gets dragged into every situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at all times, without exception, the sense of on every occasion.

clue.text: Step in to bury seed, so we hear

parts.note: to inter is to bury, and it already has the right sound and spelling

indicators.note: so we hear says the words are judged by how they are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: cede, to give up, is pronounced like seed

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to go in and plant the seed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is the word for bury exactly; only the second part changes its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to intervene on someone's behalf, which is what stepping in to help means.

clue.text: Itinerary and starting point by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is judged by its pronunciation

parts.note: a root is the origin or starting point of something

explanation.surface: Planning a journey from its plan to its point of departure.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the word for itinerary is commonly pronounced to rhyme with boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is the course or way planned for a journey, which an itinerary sets out.

clue.text: Case is trivial, if lacking four or six

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so some letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals; six, VI, uses the same two letters

explanation.surface: A legal case is dismissed as trivial unless it has some extra point.
explanation.walkthrough: Four (IV) and six (VI) are each a pair of Roman numerals sitting in the middle of the word, and dropping either gives the same result.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a court case, the hearing of a legal matter before a judge.

clue.text: Some get all shook up when broadcasters get together

definitions.note: a noun defined by a clause describing the event

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the next words is taken

parts.note: the run starts after the opening letter of the first word

explanation.surface: Elvis's All Shook Up gets played when radio presenters meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook-up is a linking of radio or television stations so they carry one shared programme.

clue.text: Edible seed taken from hick in crumpled cape

indicators.note: in places the country bumpkin inside the jumbled garment
something crumpled is crushed out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country yokel pulls something to eat from the pocket of a creased cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is a legume whose seed is eaten, for instance in hummus and curries.

clue.text: Sycophants must be small in Yemen

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the name of the country

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Flatterers in the Arabian country are said to be modest in stature.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men agree with whatever their boss says, the behaviour of fawning sycophants.

clue.text: Forerunners of public relations to escape to the South

parts.note: PR is the usual abbreviation for public relations
to elude is to escape or evade
S is the abbreviation for South, added at the end

explanation.surface: Spin doctors running off down south ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is something that comes before and introduces a larger event, so preludes are precursors.
